claims.text: Multilayer electrospark deposition using spark-plasma-sintered alloy electrodes will restore the structural integrity of damaged high-value steel components more effectively than traditional fusion-welding repair.
The proposed repair will minimize hot-cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The proposed repair will preserve favorable microstructural traits.
The steel component's microstructural sensitivity creates a high hot-cracking risk that makes traditional fusion-welding repair ineffective.
Spark plasma sintering can be used to form alloy electrodes from powders for subsequent electrospark deposition.
Multilayer electrospark deposition will create a protective, crack-resistant surface coating.
The relevant aggressive service environment includes high thermal cycling, elevated temperatures, and mechanical loads.
Electrospark deposition will form a multilayer, refined interfacial microstructure.
Electrospark deposition avoids the high heat input associated with fusion welding.
The refined interface and lower heat input mitigate the buildup of thermal stresses.
Spark plasma sintering enables alloy electrodes with controlled microstructural features.
Layered electrospark deposition produces a fine, crack-resistant interface.
The proposed process minimizes thermal gradients and associated residual stresses.
Reduced thermal gradients and residual stresses lower hot-cracking propensity.
The proposed repair will improve microstructural integrity relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The proposed repair will improve fatigue resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The proposed repair will improve tensile strength relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
Traditional fusion-welding repair of similar damaged components often causes hot-cracking.
Traditional fusion-welding repair often compromises mechanical properties under aggressive operating conditions.
